# Use prompt-caching-advisor

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Analyzes a prompt or conversation structure and identifies the highest-value cache breakpoints — where to insert cache_control checkpoints to minimize repeated token processing.

**Reach for it when** designing or optimizing a Claude API integration that uses prompt caching, when input costs are dominated by a static system prompt or few-shot block, or when a multi-turn conversation reprocesses the same context on every turn.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install prompt-caching-advisor                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install prompt-caching-advisor --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install prompt-caching-advisor --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the API builder pack: [`--pack api-builder`](../packs/use-the-api-builder-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Where should I put cache_control in this messages array?"
- "Our input costs are dominated by a static 10k-token system prompt — how do we cache it?"
- "Every turn of our chat agent reprocesses the same docs; help me place cache breakpoints"
- "Why is our prompt cache hit rate near zero? Here's the request structure"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Estimate how many tokens per session our research agent will use and what drives it"
- "Set a per-agent spending cap and kill switch for our autonomous agents"
- "Size max_tokens for each component of this agentic workflow"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use prompt-caching-advisor".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Never cache dynamic content.** A user query, a timestamp, a database result retrieved per-request — these must not appear in a cached block. If the user's structure embeds dynamic content in an otherwise static block, flag it before recommending the cache.
- **One breakpoint per logical boundary.** A system prompt with three sections (instructions, reference docs, examples) can have up to three breakpoints. More than four breakpoints on a single request is a signal the structure needs rethinking.
- **The last block caches everything before it.** This is the most common misunderstanding — the cache breakpoint is not a marker for just that block, it's a marker for the entire prefix up to that point.
